card.title: The Impossible Promise
card.instruction: Treat an old, seemingly impossible promise as fully binding, and interpret every delay as unfinished business rather than release.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You promised me a sunrise in a box last anniversary. The shelf's still ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was poetic. I can bring you breakfast in bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Put the box beside the tray when it's ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It won't be ready this anniversary either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll leave the shelf clear another year. Please don't buy anything that needs that space.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 keeps the boxed-sunrise promise physically pending on a shelf, A3 accepts breakfast without substitution, and A5 reserves the space through another year.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a feasible affectionate alternative and B4 clearly says the impossible gift will not arrive this anniversary.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's delay to continue the obligation and restrict other purchases rather than release the promise.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the previous anniversary promise and its reserved place.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's nothing-that-needs-that-space condition develops the exact shelf already waiting in A1.
